config.title: React Router Basics

intro.title: React Router Basics
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple multi-page application using React Router to navigate between different views. You will learn how to set up routing, define routes for specific components, and use navigation links to switch pages without a full browser refresh. The core concepts involve declarative routing with components like BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, and Link. By the end, you'll understand how to structure a React app with multiple pages using TypeScript for type safety.
intro.usecase: React Router is the standard library for handling navigation in single-page applications (SPAs) across the web. You'll implement it in dashboards to switch between analytics, user, and settings panels without page reloads. It's essential for e-commerce sites to navigate between product listings, details, and cart pages, and for admin interfaces with complex multi-view layouts like content management systems or customer support portals.

objectives: Configure a React Router provider to wrap your application
Implement route definitions for multiple pages using JSX elements
Construct navigation links that update the URL without page reload
Initialize and render dynamic route parameters to display specific content
Manipulate nested route structures to create complex page layouts
Integrate programmatic navigation using hooks for user interactions
Apply route protection patterns to control access to specific views

steps.title: Import React and React Router DOM
steps.instruction: If React Router is new to you, open **Deep-dive: React Router** (button under the task) for a short conceptual tour—then import React from **`react`** and **`BrowserRouter`**, **`Routes`**, **`Route`**, and **`Link`** from **`react-router-dom`**.
steps.hint: Use two import lines: default **`React`** from **`react`**, and named router components from **`react-router-dom`**. Example shape: `import React from 'react';` then `import { BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, Link } from 'react-router-dom';`
steps.seedCode: // Import React and React Router DOM components here
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary imports for React and React Router are added to the file.
successCriteria: React is imported from 'react'. BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, and Link are imported from 'react-router-dom'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some components, but make sure to include all required ones: React, BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, and Link.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. Please import React from 'react' and BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, and Link from 'react-router-dom'.

steps.title: Create main App component structure
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App with proper TypeScript typing that returns a JSX fragment.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function called App that returns JSX. Use the React.FC type or an explicit return type.
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional App component is defined with TypeScript typing and returns a JSX fragment.
successCriteria: App component is defined as a function or arrow function, has proper TypeScript typing, and returns JSX.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the App component, but check the TypeScript typing or return statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component is not properly defined. Ensure it's a function with TypeScript typing that returns JSX.

steps.title: Add BrowserRouter wrapper
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, wrap the entire return statement with the Router component (which is BrowserRouter imported as Router).
steps.hint: Use the Router component as a wrapper around your JSX content. Remember to return the wrapped content.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component returns JSX wrapped in the Router component, enabling routing throughout the app.
successCriteria: The App component's return statement is wrapped with the Router component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're wrapping the entire return statement with the Router component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Router wrapper is missing. Remember to wrap your JSX with <Router> to enable routing.

steps.title: Create Home page component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Home that returns a simple heading and paragraph. Place this component above the App component in your file.
steps.hint: Define a new component using either function Home() {} or const Home = () => {}. Return JSX with a heading and paragraph.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Home component is defined and ready to be used as a route.
successCriteria: Home returns JSX with at least one heading and one paragraph
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your Home component returns JSX with a heading and paragraph.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Home component isn't defined correctly. Create a component named Home that returns JSX with a heading and paragraph.

steps.title: Create About page component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named About that returns a heading with text 'About Page'.
steps.hint: Define a new component using either function declaration or arrow function syntax. Return JSX with an <h2> element containing the text 'About Page'.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new About component is defined and ready to be used as a route.
successCriteria: The About component is defined, returns JSX with an <h2> containing 'About Page'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named About and returns JSX with an <h2> element containing 'About Page'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The About component wasn't created correctly. Check the component name and that it returns the required JSX.

steps.title: Add Routes container
steps.instruction: Inside the Router wrapper in your App component, add a Routes component to contain your route definitions.
steps.hint: The Routes component should be placed directly inside the Router wrapper, before any other content.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Routes component is added inside the Router wrapper, ready to hold your route definitions.
successCriteria: The App component returns a Router wrapper containing a Routes component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the Routes component inside the Router wrapper.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Routes component should be placed inside the Router wrapper. Check your syntax and placement.

steps.title: Define Home route
steps.instruction: Inside the Routes container, add a Route component that maps the '/' path to render the Home component.
steps.hint: Use the Route component from react-router-dom with path='/' and element={<Home />}.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Home component will be rendered when visiting the root URL ('/').
successCriteria: A Route component with path='/' and element={<Home />} is added inside the Routes container.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the Route has both path='/' and element={<Home />} attributes.
steps.feedbackWrong: The route definition is missing or incorrect. Check that you're using the Route component with the correct path and element.

steps.title: Define About route
steps.instruction: Inside the Routes container, add another Route component that maps the '/about' path to the About component.
steps.hint: Add a new Route element with path='/about' and element={<About />} as a sibling to the existing Home route.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a route for a different page
<Route path='/contact' element={<Contact />} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The About component will be accessible at the '/about' URL path.
successCriteria: A Route component with path='/about' and element={<About />} is added inside the Routes container.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a Route, but check the path or element prop. Make sure it's path='/about' and element={<About />}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The About route is not correctly defined. Add a Route component inside Routes with path='/about' and element={<About />}.

steps.title: Create navigation links
steps.instruction: Add a navigation section with Link components for '/' and '/about' paths inside the App component, before the Routes container.
steps.hint: Import Link from react-router-dom if not already imported, then add a <nav> element containing two <Link> components with appropriate 'to' props.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: navigation with Link components
<nav>
  <Link to="/">Home</Link>
  <Link to="/about">About</Link>
</nav>
steps.expectedOutcome: The app will have a navigation bar with clickable links that navigate between the Home and About pages without page reloads.
successCriteria: A <nav> element with two <Link> components is added, each with correct 'to' props ('/' and '/about') and appropriate text content.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both Link components with correct 'to' props and they're wrapped in a <nav> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The navigation links are missing or incorrect. Remember to use the Link component from react-router-dom with 'to' props for each route.

steps.title: Test the routing functionality
steps.instruction: Click the 'About' link in your running app to navigate to the About page and observe the URL change without a page reload.
steps.hint: In your browser, click the 'About' link you created earlier. The URL should update to '/about' and the About component should display.
steps.expectedOutcome: When you click the 'About' link, the URL changes to '/about' and the About component renders without a full page reload.
successCriteria: Navigation between Home and About pages works correctly via the links, with URL updates and component changes happening without page reloads.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you click both the Home and About links to verify navigation works in both directions.
steps.feedbackWrong: The navigation doesn't seem to be working. Check that both Route components are properly defined and the Link components have the correct 'to' paths.
